newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields off highs on overseas, crown.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields off highs on overseas, crown.

text.p: Swedish debt yields came off morning highs, tracking European yields lower, and supported by a stronger crown which firmed on commercial flows.

European yields shook off renewed fears of a U.S. rate hike. The market focus remained on the FOMC meeting on May 20 and on statements from the Swedish government about its stance on the European economic and monetary union.
Yields rose Wednesday morning after an article in Swedish daily Svenska Dagbladet saying that Prime Minister Goran Persson and Finance Minister Erik Asbrink were negative towards EMU.
The market is also eyeing U.S. PPI due at 1230 GMT and U.S. CPI on Thursday.

Six month T-bill rate was two basis points higher at 4.20 percent and the ten year bond yield was up three basis points at 7.03 percent after having touched 7.07 percent. The crown firmed to 4.4970 crowns to the mark versus 4.5175 crowns on Tuesday.
